newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt blames Israel for Syrian suspicions.
newsitem.headline: Egypt blames Israel for Syrian suspicions.

text.p: Egypt said on Friday the Israeli government was responsible for a breakdown of trust with Syria because it wanted to backtrack on the position former prime minister Yitzhak Rabin took on the Golan Heights.

President Hosni Mubarak, in a New Year's interview with state television, also said Israel had tried to make Egypt force the Palestinians to accept Israeli conditions in negotiations on the West Bank town of Hebron.

"Our brothers in Syria now have no trust in Israel at all," Mubarak said. "And Israel is the reason because there are agreements which haven't been carried out and haven't been honoured -- contrary to what we hear from them (the Israelis)."
He made no mention of a bomb attack in Damascus on Tuesday which Syria blamed on Israeli agents, bringing already poor relations between the two to another low.

Mubarak repeated his account of the state of negotiations on the Golan Heights under Rabin, saying the late prime minister was ready to give back all Syrian territory and wanted only to know what Syria would give in return.
"I don't believe that our brothers in Lebanon or Syria will start talks unless they have in front of them something to give confidence in the talks," he said.

"Syria says it is ready to start talks from the point they had reached but they (the Israeli government of prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu) said we don't know, there's nothing written on paper. But there are some documents saying they talked about the Golan and there are witnesses to that and (to the fact) that they were ready to give the Golan back," he added.

"They just wanted to know what they would get in return...I spoke to (Syrian President) Hafez al-Assad and he didn't say no and he didn't say yes. I took that as a sign that there was scope for some thinking," he said.

Mubarak, explaining a recent tiff in Egypt's bilateral relationship with Israel, said that on a visit to Cairo late last year Netanyahu's adviser Dore Gold complained that Egypt was complicating U.S. mediation in the Hebron negotiations.
"I was amazed. It meant (Israel wanted us to) bring the Palestinians and tell them to accept what the Israelis have offered and sign and carry it out.
"How can that be? So that we can then be insulted? And that we should be the traitors who sold out the Palestinian cause? That's what it was about," Mubarak added.
The Egyptian president said that progress towards peace between Israel and the Palestinians was essential to talks with Syria because it would help restore confidence.

"I hope with all my heart that what was agreed must be respected because that's the key for you to speak with Syria. Without that Syria will not have trust signing anything with Israel or even negotiating with Israel," he said.
On the Hebron agreement, which is still under negotiation, Mubarak said the Israelis must simultaneously set a timetable for all the redeployments from the West Bank.

"When they (the Israelis) say let's not set a date for the end of the redeployment, this creates more fears that they want to redeploy one or two km (miles) and then stop. That fits in with the rumour that the Israelis don't want to do anything other than Hebron," he said.

"But any setback or violation and failure to agree on the agreement, the Israelis must understand that will not lead to peace, it will lead to violence, it will lead to wrecking the peace process," he added.
"I hope that this year, and it's essential, that we reach peace. The Palestinian question must move in the right direction. I do have confidence and I'm by nature optimistic."
